You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 4527025d440ce84bf56e75ce1df2e84cb8178616 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 12:33:34 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] nfc: nci: fix circular locking dependency in nci_close_device

nci_close_device() flushes rx_wq and tx_wq while holding req_lock.
This causes a circular locking dependency because nci_rx_work()
running on rx_wq can end up taking req_lock too:

  nci_rx_work -> nci_rx_data_packet -> nci_data_exchange_complete
    -> __sk_destruct -> rawsock_destruct -> nfc_deactivate_target
    -> nci_deactivate_target -> nci_request -> mutex_lock(&ndev->req_lock)

Move the flush of rx_wq after req_lock has been released.
This should safe (I think) because NCI_UP has already been cleared
and the transport is closed, so the work will see it and return
-ENETDOWN.

NIPA has been hitting this running the nci selftest with a debug
kernel on roughly 4% of the runs.

Fixes: 6a2968aaf50c ("NFC: basic NCI protocol implementation")
Reviewed-by: Ian Ray <ian.ray@gehealthcare.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260317193334.988609-1-kuba@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/nfc/nci/core.c b/net/nfc/nci/core.c
index 43d871525dbc..5f46c4b5720f 100644
--- a/net/nfc/nci/core.c
+++ b/net/nfc/nci/core.c
@@ -579,8 +579,7 @@ static int nci_close_device(struct nci_dev *ndev)
 	skb_queue_purge(&ndev->rx_q);
 	skb_queue_purge(&ndev->tx_q);
 
-	/* Flush RX and TX wq */
-	flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq);
+	/* Flush TX wq, RX wq flush can't be under the lock */
 	flush_workqueue(ndev->tx_wq);
 
 	/* Reset device */
@@ -592,13 +591,13 @@ static int nci_close_device(struct nci_dev *ndev)
 		      msecs_to_jiffies(NCI_RESET_TIMEOUT));
 
 	/* After this point our queues are empty
-	 * and no works are scheduled.
+	 * rx work may be running but will see that NCI_UP was cleared
 	 */
 	ndev->ops->close(ndev);
 
 	clear_bit(NCI_INIT, &ndev->flags);
 
-	/* Flush cmd wq */
+	/* Flush cmd and tx wq */
 	flush_workqueue(ndev->cmd_wq);
 
 	timer_delete_sync(&ndev->cmd_timer);
@@ -613,6 +612,9 @@ static int nci_close_device(struct nci_dev *ndev)
 
 	mutex_unlock(&ndev->req_lock);
 
+	/* rx_work may take req_lock via nci_deactivate_target */
+	flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq);
+
 	return 0;
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `net/nfc/nci/core.c`

1. **Removed `flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq)` from the locked section**  
   - The original code flushed `rx_wq` and `tx_wq` while holding `req_lock`. The flush of `rx_wq` was deleted from this location.

2. **Updated comments**  
   - Changed comment from "Flush RX and TX wq" to "Flush TX wq, RX wq flush can't be under the lock".  
   - Updated comment after reset to note that `rx_wq` may still be running but will see `NCI_UP` cleared.  
   - Corrected comment after `clear_bit(NCI_INIT)` from "Flush cmd wq" to "Flush cmd and tx wq" (actually only `cmd_wq` is flushed there, but the comment was adjusted to mention cmd and tx; note: `tx_wq` was already flushed earlier).

3. **Added `flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq)` after `mutex_unlock`**  
   - The flush of `rx_wq` is moved to after the release of `req_lock`, ensuring no circular lock dependency occurs.

### Relationships Between Changes

- The core issue is a circular locking dependency: `nci_close_device` flushed `rx_wq` while holding `req_lock`, but `nci_rx_work` (running on `rx_wq`) can end up acquiring `req_lock` through a call chain (`nci_rx_work → nci_rx_data_packet → nci_data_exchange_complete → __sk_destruct → rawsock_destruct → nfc_deactivate_target → nci_deactivate_target → nci_request → mutex_lock(&ndev->req_lock)`).  

- The fix breaks this cycle by moving the flush of `rx_wq` outside the `req_lock` critical section. This is safe because `NCI_UP` has already been cleared and the transport is closed before releasing the lock, so any pending work on `rx_wq` will immediately return `-ENETDOWN` without needing the lock.  

- The comment updates reflect the new reasoning and ensure maintainers understand why `rx_wq` is flushed later, outside the lock.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq);  // called while mutex_lock(&ndev->req_lock) is held
mutex_lock(&ndev->req_lock);   // inside nci_request, called from nci_rx_work path

Reason:
nci_close_device() acquires req_lock and then flushes the rx_wq workqueue, waiting for all pending work to complete. However, nci_rx_work can trigger a sequence that eventually calls nci_request, which tries to acquire the same req_lock. This creates a circular dependency: the lock holder waits for the workqueue, and the work waits for the lock, leading to a deadlock.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
mutex_unlock(&ndev->req_lock);
flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq);

Reason:
By moving the flush of rx_wq after releasing req_lock, the lock is no longer held when waiting for rx_wq completion. Since NCI_UP is already cleared and the transport is closed, any pending rx_work will see the shutdown state and return early without trying to take req_lock, breaking the circular dependency.
